test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 12 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Of the given options, which is the saltiest sea in the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Red sea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Red Sea **is a confined body of water that stretches** 1,930 kilometres southeast from** **Suez, Egypt, to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, **where it joins the Gulf of Aden and, ultimately, the Arabian Sea.
 
• **The Gulf of Aqaba (Elat) and the Gulf of Suez** must be viewed geologically as the northern extension of the same structure.
 
• The coasts of Saudi Arabia and Yemen are to the east, while those of Egypt, Sudan, and Eritrea are to the west.
 
• It has a maximum width of 190 miles, a maximum depth of** 3,040 metres (9,974 ft), and an area of over 174,000 miles (450,000 square km). Some of the world's saltiest and hottest waters can be found in the Red Sea.**
 
• It is one of the busiest waterways in the world, bringing maritime traffic between **Europe and Asia and connecting to the Mediterranean Sea via the Suez Canal.**
 
• **Its name comes from the colour shifts in its waters that have been noticed.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **The North and Central European Plain, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Russia, and Sweden** all enclose the Baltic Sea, which is a branch of the Atlantic Ocean.
 
• **The Sulu Archipelago, Sulu Sea, and Mindanao Island in the Philippines, the Sangihe Islands series, Sulawesi's Minahasa Peninsula, northern Kalimantan in Indonesia, and the western Pacific Ocean's Celebes Sea **all abut the sea on the Celebes Sea's northern and western edges, respectively.
 
• **A peripheral Mediterranean sea of the Atlantic Ocean, the Black Sea is located between Europe and Asia, east of the Balkans, south of the East European Plain, west of the Caucasus, and north of Anatolia.**
